\[
\boxed{\left(3,\frac13\right)}
\]

Let the replacement matrix be
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}
9&3&0\\
1&7&4\\
2&2&8
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Each row sums to \(12\), so the total number of balls after \(n\) draws is
\[
T_n=12(n+1).
\]
The limiting composition vector is
\[
\pi=\left(\frac13,\frac13,\frac13\right),
\]
since \(\pi A=12\pi\). Put
\[
Y_n=X_n-T_n\pi.
\]
Then \(Y_n\) always lies in the plane \(r+g+b=0\), and \(\operatorname{Cov}(X_n)=\operatorname{Cov}(Y_n)\).

The eigenvalues of \(A\) are
\[
12,\quad 6,\quad 6,
\]
because
\[
\det(\lambda I-A)=(\lambda-12)(\lambda-6)^2.
\]
The eigenvalue \(6\) is defective. Choose
\[
q_1=(1,-1,0)^T,\qquad q_2=\left(\frac13,0,-\frac13\right)^T,
\]
so that
\[
Aq_1=6q_1,\qquad Aq_2=6q_2+q_1.
\]
Define
\[
z_{1,n}=Y_nq_1,\qquad z_{2,n}=Y_nq_2.
\]
Since \(T_n=12(n+1)\), the linearized recurrences are exactly
\[
z_{1,n+1}=\left(1+\frac1{2(n+1)}\right)z_{1,n}+e_{1,n+1},
\]
\[
z_{2,n+1}=\left(1+\frac1{2(n+1)}\right)z_{2,n}
+\frac1{12(n+1)}z_{1,n}+e_{2,n+1},
\]
where \(e_{i,n+1}\) are centered martingale increments.

At equilibrium, the three possible replacement increments minus their mean \((4,4,4)\) are
\[
(5,-1,-4),\quad (-3,3,0),\quad (-2,-2,4).
\]
For \(q_1=(1,-1,0)^T\), the corresponding values are
\[
6,\quad -6,\quad 0,
\]
so
\[
S_{11}:=\lim \operatorname{Var}(e_{1,n+1}\mid\mathcal F_n)
=\frac{6^2+(-6)^2+0^2}{3}=24.
\]

Let \(L=\log n\). The defective Jordan term contributes a factor
\[
\frac1{12}\log(n/k)
\]
from \(z_1\)-noise into \(z_2\). Therefore
\[
\operatorname{Var}(z_{1,n})\sim 24\,nL,
\]
\[
\operatorname{Cov}(z_{1,n},z_{2,n})\sim
24n\sum_{k\le n}\frac1k\cdot \frac1{12}\log(n/k)
\sim nL^2,
\]
and
\[
\operatorname{Var}(z_{2,n})
\sim
24n\sum_{k\le n}\frac1k\cdot \frac1{144}\log^2(n/k)
\sim \frac1{18}nL^3.
\]
Thus the covariance matrix of \((z_{1,n},z_{2,n})\) has leading form
\[
K_n\sim
\begin{pmatrix}
24nL & nL^2\\
nL^2 & \frac1{18}nL^3
\end{pmatrix},
\]
so
\[
\det K_n\sim
\left(24\cdot\frac1{18}-1\right)n^2L^4
=\frac13 n^2L^4.
\]

Now convert back to the physical plane \(r+g+b=0\). The dual basis vectors satisfying \(Y=z_1r_1+z_2r_2\) are
\[
r_1=\left(\frac13,-\frac23,\frac13\right),\qquad
r_2=(1,1,-2).
\]
The largest covariance direction is \(r_2\), hence
\[
\lambda_n^+\sim \frac1{18}nL^3\|r_2\|^2
=\frac1{18}nL^3\cdot 6
=\frac13 nL^3.
\]
Also
\[
\det(R^TR)=
\begin{vmatrix}
\frac23 & -1\\
-1 & 6
\end{vmatrix}
=3,
\]
so the product of the two nonzero eigenvalues is
\[
\lambda_n^-\lambda_n^+
\sim 3\det K_n
\sim n^2L^4.
\]
Therefore
\[
\lambda_n^-\sim \frac{n^2L^4}{(1/3)nL^3}=3nL.
\]

Hence
\[
\boxed{\left(
\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\lambda_n^-}{n\log n},
\;
\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\lambda_n^+}{n(\log n)^3}
\right)
=
\left(3,\frac13\right)}.
\]
